title: Smart routing fallback - incident breadcrumbs (Ethan Park)
content:
Top-level summary:
- Short: saw a cluster of user-facing errors when smart-routing attempted regional failover to eu-west-1 during a capacity blip in us-east-1. Fallback policy triggered but some requests failed with 502/503 or hung (timeouts).
- Impact: ~1.8% of traffic for the org-route 'chat/default' experienced degraded responses for ~11 minutes (2026-02-28 01:12-01:23 UTC).

Timeline / breadcrumbs (notes to self):
- 2026-02-28 01:10 UTC: increased 95th latency in us-east-1 per route dashboard (console).
- 01:12 UTC: router policy detected capacity-constrained in us-east-1 and began routing 20% of traffic to fallback region (eu-west-1) per canary policy.
- 01:13-01:18 UTC: error spike: 502/503 and request timeouts observed in eu-west-1.
- 01:20 UTC: automation scaled dedicated pool in eu-west-1 but errors persisted for a few more minutes.
- 01:23 UTC: errors subsided; rollback to primary routing completed by 01:25.

Commands I ran (repro / quick checks):
- Check router health / decision logs (local reproduce):
  kubectl -n serving logs deploy/smart-router -c router --since=20m | grep "route_decision" | tail -n 200
  -> saw a bunch of records with "decision=fallback" and decision_latency_ms ~ 10-30ms then later "decision=failover"

- Inspect fallback-service errors in eu-west-1:
  kubectl -n serving logs deploy/fallback-proxy -c proxy --since=30m | grep "ERROR" | head -n 50
  -> repeated: "ERROR fallback-proxy: upstream_connect error: connection refused\n" and occasional: "kv-cache-miss: missing model-id for variant redwood-3b-quant-eu"

- Health endpoints:
  curl -sS https://eu-west-1.fallback.redwood-inference.internal/healthz | jq .
  -> {"ok":false,"reason":"model-mapping-missing"}  (consistent with logs)

- Quick inference test to primary vs fallback (from my laptop via curl to edge):
  curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x...' -d '{"route":"chat/default","input":"hi"}'
  -> when routed to eu-west-1: stalled, then 502. When routed to us-east-1: success but high latency (~800ms).

Relevant log snippets (sanitized):
- smart-router:
  [2026-02-28T01:13:04Z] INFO route_decision route=chat/default user=acct-34 decision=fallback target=eu-west-1 reason="capacity:us-east-1:exhausted"
  [2026-02-28T01:13:04Z] ERROR route_exec route=chat/default request_id=rid-abc123 error="upstream_connect: connection refused"

- fallback-proxy:
  [2026-02-28T01:13:05Z] ERROR proxy::connect upstream=platform-eu-01:443 error=ConnectionRefused
  [2026-02-28T01:13:05Z] WARN model_mapper model_id=redwood-3b-quant-eu status=not_found
  [2026-02-28T01:14:10Z] ERROR kv-cache-miss key=variant-map:chat/default:eu-west-1

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model mapping / deployment gap in eu-west-1 for some variants. Logs show "model-mapping-missing" and kv-cache misses which would cause fallback proxy to be unable to forward to a local model server -> 502/503.
2) Short-lived capacity/placement issue caused router to push traffic before all fallback-shards were warm, leading to connection refused while pool spun up. Autoscaler later filled the pool, reducing failures.
3) Network partition between fallback-proxy and model runtime (less likely given model-mapping logs).
4) Race/ordering bug: routing decision stored before model mapping refreshed in KV. We saw decision logs followed immediately by kv-cache-miss entries.

What we tried (mitigations / experiments):
- Temporarily increased canary warm-up delay from 10s -> 60s for route chat/default (console) to ensure fallback pool fully provisioned before routed traffic. Observed fewer errors on subsequent small tests.
- Manually pushed missing model mapping in kv-store for eu-west-1 (kv-tool set variant-map:chat/default '{"variant":"redwood-3b-quant-eu"}') - after this, healthz returned ok and proxy errors dropped. Need to verify persisted mapping source.
- Added defensive checks in fallback-proxy to return 429 (backoff) instead of 502 when model mapping missing - reduced noisy 502s in SRE runbook tests.

Open questions / follow-ups (next actions):
- Why was mapping missing? Is there a flaky deploy job that occasionally fails to register variants in region on model rollout? Check model-onboarding job logs around 00:30-01:00 UTC. (Assigned Marcus)
- Add stronger preflight: router should check mapping readiness for a route+variant before sending non-zero traffic. If mapping incomplete, either delay or send to a safe fallback variant. (Product + Eng discussion)
- Improve observability: add metric "model_mapping_ready" by region+variant and surface in console with alert if <100% readiness for a route. (Assigned Olivia)
- Run canary tests that exercise both a cold start and mapping propagation for every new variant/region. (SRE/Release)
- Confirm kv-store persistence: ensure manual kv-tool writes survive restart / are part of deployment templating. (Amara)

Reproduction steps (dev sandbox):
1) Deploy a new variant to us-east-1 only (simulate missing registration for eu-west-1).
2) Flip router policy to route 30% traffic to eu-west-1 canary.
3) Observe fallback-proxy errors and kv-cache-miss logs.
4) Run kv-tool set mapping -> watch backlog clear.

Quick TO-DO (notes for ticket JIRA-ENG-9876):
- [ ] Add mapping readiness check in router (ethan)
- [ ] Postmortem draft for incident (include timeline + mitigation) (olivia)
- [ ] Fix model-onboarding job to retry on transient failures (marcus)
- [ ] Add alert and dashboard for "model_mapping_ready" (product + sre)
- [ ] Add e2e canary that validates mapping propagation before routing (release)

Random stray notes / heuristics I keep in mind:
- Fallback-first should be conservative: prefer slower but reliable fallback over pushing to an unready region.
- When seeing "connection refused" + "model-not-found" logs together, 90% of time it's a registration/mapping problem not a network outage.
- For future incidents, capture first 2 minutes of smart-router trace + mapping KV diffs immediately (automate snapshot).

If we want, I can cut this into a short postmortem skeleton. For now leaving as raw breadcrumbs so the team can iterate quickly.
